summary: Lamar Jackson is out, so Tyler Huntley (8-9 career starter) faces a Browns offense that is last in success rate; sharp money hit the Under and Cleveland. Most likely to win: Baltimore Ravens ML.

legs.note: Cleveland's offense ranks near the bottom in success rate, and Huntley plus Henry should shorten the game.

extra_legs.note: Baltimore is 4-1, Huntley keeps winning fill-in starts, and Cleveland's offense struggles to score.

extra_legs.status: consensus BAL -3 (VegasInsider/CBS); +3.5 quoted at DK (SBR) and Covers -3.5; may be gone by kickoff
extra_legs.note: With a sub-40 total and a backup QB, a game decided by three points or fewer is very live.

research:
1) QBs/personnel: Lamar Jackson (left ankle sprain, Week 4 vs Titans, no practice since 10/4) OUT, announced Friday by HC Jesse Minter (ESPN, NFL.com, CBS). Tyler Huntley makes his 13th Ravens start; he is 3-0 in his recent fill-in starts, including the 30-23 OT win at ATL on 10/11 (24/32, 201 yds, 2 TD, 11/11 on the final two drives, walk-off 1-yd TD run; AP). 2026 season: about 52/67, 426 yds, 2 TD, 0 INT, 151 rush yds (StatSniper/FanDuel). Browns QB Deshaun Watson: 1,010 yds, 7 TD, 2 INT in 5 games, 69.6% comp, 7.4 YPA, 94.1 rating, but a 52.9 PFF grade (32nd of 36). Went 15/33 for 155 yds in the 17-12 loss at NYJ, sacked 8 times, strip-sack to end it. Monken is sticking with Watson. Derrick Henry: league-high 113 carries, 476 yds (95.2 ypg), 24-102 vs ATL.
2) Injuries (Friday reports): BAL lists 21 players. OUT: Jackson, C Cam Jurgens, Matt Hibner, DT Broderick Washington. Q: G Andrew Vorhees, G Emery Jones, WR Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist, likely plays). Trey Hendrickson (finger) full. CLE has 17 listed, 5 out and 4 questionable. OUT: Teven Jenkins (back), DT Mike Hall Jr. (ankle), Dillon Gabriel (back). Q: LB Carson Schwesinger (ankle), DT Mason Graham, DE Derek Barnett, RB Quinshon Judkins (all ankle). Sunday inactives not confirmed (search budget exhausted).
3) Advanced: Browns offense 23rd in EPA/play (-0.084, NextLevelStats) and 35% success rate since 2025, worst in the NFL (BetMGM). Ravens D is 16th (-0.02, Muffed) or -0.06 (Sumer), and best vs play-action (-0.49 EPA). Browns D is just outside the top 10 in EPA and DVOA (Covers), but 29th in opp rush EPA and 28th in rush success rate (SI), allowing 117.4 rush ypg.
4) Scheme: Expect a Henry-heavy plan with Huntley's legs, against a Browns interior missing Hall and possibly Graham. The CLE offense struggles under pass rush (8 sacks vs NYJ), and BAL has Hendrickson healthy.
5) Coaching: Browns HC Todd Monken was Ravens OC for the previous three seasons, so he knows the personnel. Minter (BAL, first year) is managing Lamar conservatively.
6) Situational: Divisional game. BAL is 4-1 and leads the AFC North by a game. CLE is 3-2 after a 3-game win streak ended in the rain at NYJ. Week labeled 6 by most outlets.
7) History: Browns 6-4 ATS in the last 10 meetings, and the over is 5-0 in the last 5 meetings (SI/FanDuel preview).
8) Weather: Dry, 56-62F, wind 7-8 mph with possible gusts of 15-25+ (Sharp, MySportsWeather, Fox 8). Minor impact.
9) Market/experts: The look-ahead with Lamar was BAL -6.5/44.5. Consensus is now BAL -3/39.5 (VegasInsider; books at 39.5-40.5), with some books at -3.5/-4.5. ML: BAL -166/CLE +140 (NBC) or -175/+145 (ESPN). WagerTalk reports 89% of money on the Under vs 74% of tickets on the Over. Picks: Covers' Tom Oldfield, BAL -3.5. Covers' Jason Logan, BAL -4.5 and Under 41.5 (early). Covers ATS column, CLE if Huntley starts. Sportsbook Review, CLE +3.5 -105 (DK). bet365, BAL ML -167 and Over 39.5 -109. TheRx, Under 40. SportsGambler, Over 39.5 -105. SI, BAL -4.5 -107. Yahoo, BAL 31-17 (bold) and an Anthony/Spencer split of CLE 24-17 and BAL 27-20. The Banner staff mostly picks BAL (27-20). Props: Henry o88.5 (Covers) and o89.5 -103 (SI), both lean over. Note: the web search budget ran out after 17 searches, so team-total prices and Watson prop lines could not be found and are omitted. Fetch of odds pages failed (DNS), so prices come from search snapshots.

SECOND PASS (12 more searches):
1b) Huntley track record: 7-9 career record as a starter before 2026 (11 BAL starts, 5 MIA; Field Level Media, May 2026). Career 66.2% comp, about 3,275 yds, 13 TD, 10 INT, 82.7 rating, 811 rush yds (Wikipedia). 2024 MIA: 829 yds, 3 TD, 3 INT, 80.1 rating. Now 8-9 after the ATL win, and has won his last three starts (ESPN). 2026: 32/41, 264 yds, 2 TD, 0 INT in 2 games (FanDuel Research). FanDuel pass-yds prop is 161.5 (price not found, so no leg).
2b) Inactives and Mason Graham: official inactives not yet posted. Graham (MCL and ankle sprains from Week 4, missed Week 5) was DNP Wed/Thu, limited Fri, questionable. Cabot (cleveland.com) gives him a 'decent shot'. CLE elevated DTs Sam Kamara and Chris Williams Saturday, with Hall and Kalia Davis also out. Judkins was upgraded to limited Friday and is questionable. BAL C Cam Jurgens is out (concussion).
3b) Pass D: CLE allows 216.6 pass ypg (13th) and hasn't allowed a 300-yd passer in 50 straight games. BAL allows 223.6 pass ypg (18th) and 5 pass TD.
8b) Weather: DraftKings Network shows sunny, 58F, S wind 8 mph, 0% rain, low impact. Fantasy Alarm shows gusts of 14-15 mph. KickoffWeather shows 10-20 mph.
9b) Line movement/money: BetMGM opened BAL -6.5/43.5, now -4.5/41.5 (Rotowire). Total went 44.5 to 41.5 with 19% of tickets and 31% of money on the Under (TheOddsBreakers). Sharps were on CLE +4.5/+4 (Yahoo). Consensus now -3/39.5 (CBS, VegasInsider). BetMGM had 40.5 with the Under at -145. More picks after the Lamar news: Pete Prisco (CBS), BAL 24-13. Jordan Dajani (CBS), BAL 26-20. SportsLine AI, Under 39.5 and BAL -3. numberFire model gives BAL a 61.4% win probability. SBR projects BAL 20-17 with CLE +3.5 and Under 41.5. Watson averages 202 ypg, a coin flip, so no leg.
